logp.method_description: The complexes were first dissolved in DMSO, followed by dilution in PBS to achieve a final DMSO concentration < 1%. Immediately upon dissolution, the samples were measured using a Thermo Scientific Evolution 260 Bio UV–Vis spectrophotometer where the absorbance spectrum was collected from 800 nm to 220 nm. Next, the PBS solution of each complex was combined with an equal volume of 1-octanol and the resulting bi-phasic solution was mixed using an IKA Trayster digital inversion mixer for 30 min. Following mixing the layers were separated via centrifugation. The aqueous layer was drawn off and the absorbance was measured again. The difference in absorbance values at the λmax before and after mixing was used to determine the log D7.4 of each complex, using the equation below: Log D7.4 = log[(Abs at λmax before mixing / Abs at λmax after mixing) - 1]

Each Ru complex was first dissolved in DMSO and then diluted using phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) to achieve a 50 uM solution containing 1% DMSO. The absorbance of the resultant aqueous solution was measured, then an equal volume of 1-octanol was added, and the two phases were mixed using an IKA Trayster digital mixer for 30 min at 60 rpm under ambient conditions. After mixing, the sample was briefly centrifuged (3 min, 4900 rpm) and the aqueous layer was carefully removed, and the absorbance spectrum was measured. Mixing was limited to 30 min so that the parent complex, rather than its ligand-exchange products, is the partitioning species.
